completionPolicy: Existing guided-attempt rule; construction and explanation are supported here. No optional model/investigation becomes required. Correct answers are not required for an attempt.
saveContract: Graph coordinates, axis choices and explanation encode together in this existing response field. Preserve prior plain writing visibly; do not silently replace it.
learnerWorkflow: Read the supplied data and identify what is measured.
Choose the horizontal label, vertical label and vertical maximum.
Enter each plotted value using keyboard-accessible numeric controls; the graph must reflect entered values, not automatically filled source answers.
Compare only after attempting; identify missing points, wrong values and scale limits without silently correcting them.
Explain the biological comparison, then save the complete construction.
rendererRequirements: All numeric fields have series, x-position and unit labels. Keyboard operation does not require dragging.
Show all supplied values in an adjacent accessible table.
Show any point outside the selected scale as an explicit warning and in the data table; never silently crop it.
Keep blanks distinct from zero, and keep unfinished graph drafts recoverable.
Read-only model-answer figures stay hidden until attempted.
All My Work derives readable axes, every entered point and the explanation from this same saved response; return focus to this activity.
Numerical x positions must use proportional spacing: cycle days 12–14 cannot have the same gap as days 14–21. Categorical bars use equal category spacing.
A larger scale that contains the data is not an incorrect answer. Explain its resolution trade-off and warn when the scale is too small.

source.qualification: Illustrative classification counts, not newly collected microscopy observations or measured phase times.

modelExplanation: Mitotic index is 28/100=28%. Time estimates also need a known cycle length and a representative, roughly steady, asynchronously dividing population without major stage-specific loss. A high phase count can reflect delayed progression.
